title: Editor crashes when minimized on Windows with Compatibility renderer and an old Intel chipset
body: I can reproduce this in Godot 4.3 rc2 on Windows 10 using OpenGL3 Compatibility. When I open a project and minimize Godot, including while it is starting, while debug is open, or while the editor is open, it crashes. Minimizing it twice leaves Godot.exe unresponsive.

symptoms_visible: Godot 4.3 rc2 crashes or stops responding when I minimize it on Windows 10 with the OpenGL3 Compatibility renderer.
I can reproduce it by opening a project and minimizing Godot twice, and I have also seen it while Godot is starting or a debug session is open.
N0.label: N0 minimize crash reported

symptoms_visible: An empty Compatibility project crashes as soon as I minimize Godot on the affected old Intel graphics systems.
The same machines do not crash when minimized with Godot 4.3 rc1 or the tested 4.2 releases, while 4.3 rc2 and rc3 do.
Windows records an access violation in ig8icd64.dll when the process closes.
N1.label: N1 old Intel regression established

symptoms_visible: The minimize crash remains reproducible in the debug build on an affected Intel system.
WinDbg stops on an access violation inside ig8icd64.dll, with the Godot frames below it including RasterizerGLES3::_blit_render_target_to_screen.
N2.label: N2 debug call stack collected

symptoms_visible: The tested revisions switch from not crashing to crashing within the 4.3 rc1-to-rc2 range when I minimize the editor.
N3.label: N3 regression bisected

symptoms_visible: The provided CI build works on the affected old Intel machines and no longer crashes when Godot is minimized.
N4.label: N4 candidate correction verified

symptoms_visible: With a build containing the correction for the bisected Windows subwindow change, I can minimize Godot normally without the editor, project manager, or running project crashing.
N_terminal.label: terminal minimize crash resolved

question_patterns: What exact CPU, GPU, and graphics driver are on the affected machine?
Please use Help > Copy System Info and share the resulting system and renderer details.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce this on old Intel graphics systems that use Compatibility mode. One is Intel Iris Graphics 6100 with driver 10.18.15.4279 on Windows 10, and another affected machine uses Intel HD Graphics 405. These systems do not support the normal Vulkan renderer.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can reproduce it on current NVIDIA and AMD systems too, including in Forward+, and none of the affected machines use Intel graphics.
The Intel driver has the same generation and behavior but a slightly different OEM revision number.

question_patterns: Does it also crash if you create an empty 2D project in Compatibility mode and only minimize the editor?
Can you reproduce this in a blank Compatibility project without your project content?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I created a new Compatibility project, did nothing except minimize Godot, and it crashed. I reopened the same empty project and minimizing it crashed again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, an empty project never crashes; it only happens in my main project while a specific scene and plug-in are active.

question_patterns: Does the same minimize action crash in Godot 4.3 rc1 or the 4.2 releases?
Which earlier and later release candidates reproduce this on the same computer?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On the same hardware, 4.3 rc1 definitely does not crash. I also checked 4.2, 4.2.1, and 4.2.2 without reproducing it. The crash occurs in 4.3 rc2 and still occurs in 4.3 rc3.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It also crashes identically in 4.2 and 4.3 rc1, so there is no rc1-to-rc2 regression.
4.2.1 and 4.3 rc1 are good while rc2 and rc3 are bad, but I did not separately test 4.2.2.

question_patterns: Can you launch Godot from a terminal with verbose output and check what remains after the crash?
What does Windows Event Viewer record for the faulting module and exception code?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Event Viewer reports Godot terminating with exception code 0xc0000005. The faulting module is C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\ig8icd64.dll, version 10.18.15.4279. Both the Godot window and command window close without warning.

edges.comment: Thread c3-c11, c20, c23, c25-c26. The original reporter supplied the fourth-generation Intel context; Snowlette and ahopness supplied exact affected Intel configurations, empty-project reproduction, Event Viewer output, and the version matrix. These affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the crash using the provided development build and capture its call stack in WinDbg?
Please test the build with debug symbols and paste the raw exception and stack output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it with the debug build and opened it in WinDbg. It reports access violation c0000005 in ig8icd64!DrvSetLayerPaletteEntries. The stack then reaches Godot through RasterizerGLES3::_blit_render_target_to_screen at rasterizer_gles3.cpp:418, followed by blit_render_targets_to_screen and RendererViewport::draw_viewports.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The debug build crashes before rendering starts, and the stack contains only a C# plug-in and CoreCLR frames with no Intel OpenGL or GLES3 calls.
The same ig8icd64 and RasterizerGLES3 frames appear, but WinDbg reports a different offset inside the Intel module.

edges.comment: Thread c12-c18 and c20. Alex2782 supplied debug builds; ahopness reproduced the crash on the affected Intel HD Graphics 405 system and pasted the raw WinDbg and symbolized call stacks. Snowlette's separate test of an earlier custom build did not crash, but it was not the final corrective build.

question_patterns: Can you bisect the minimize crash between the last working 4.3 rc1 revision and the first crashing 4.3 rc2 revision?
Please compile and test revisions between the known-working and known-crashing builds, then paste the raw git bisect output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I bisected between 4.3 rc1 as good and 4.3 rc2 as bad. The final output marks 97aa278edbade56e0554c97fc03cd8ea20282c62, titled 'Pass window exclusive and transient properties for subwindow creation', as BAD. The preceding tested revision 6a1ac99a981afa0b7aaa362e5314b74411a741b0 was GOOD, while the revisions after it in my run were BAD.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisection instead identifies an unrelated GLES3 shader compiler change as the first bad revision, before any subwindow-property change.
The same subwindow-property revision is the first bad result, but I used full commit hashes for the rc1 and rc2 endpoints.

edges.comment: Thread c21-c22 and c28, c38-c40. Snowlette performed the requested source build bisection on the affected Iris Graphics 6100 laptop and pasted the raw GOOD/BAD sequence. Identifying the first-bad change as the relevant Godot regression is engineer-side interpretation consumed by the final solution.

question_patterns: Please test the provided CI build on the same affected machine and tell me what happens when you minimize Godot.
Can you repeatedly minimize the editor, project manager, and a running project with this candidate build and report whether they still crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the provided CI build on the affected old Intel systems. It is working fine: minimizing Godot no longer crashes on my machine. A second affected machine also passed a limited minimize test without crashing.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The provided CI build still crashes in ig8icd64.dll every time I minimize the empty Compatibility project.
The build survives repeated editor minimization, but I only performed a short test of the project manager.

edges.comment: Thread c41-c43. Alvinhochun requested testing of the new candidate and akien-mga linked its CI artifact. Ahopness confirmed it worked on the affected Intel HD Graphics 405 machine; Snowlette had also confirmed the related test direction on the affected Iris 6100 system. Both affected users are folded into the simulated user response.

solution.intent: Apply the correction for the Windows subwindow-creation regression isolated by the bisection, rather than treating the minimize crash as solely an unavoidable old Intel driver failure.
solution.concrete_example: Use a Godot build containing the maintainer's correction for the problem in the bisected change that began passing exclusive and transient properties during subwindow creation. The candidate CI build was tested successfully on affected old Intel Compatibility systems.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied raw version tests, the WinDbg stack, and a git-bisect sequence ending at the subwindow-property change. Concluding that this change contains the relevant Godot-side regression—and that the old Intel OpenGL driver is the environment in which it manifests rather than a complete explanation by itself—is the maintainer's inference. The thread does not describe the internal contents of the linked correction in enough detail to score a more specific mechanism.

edges.comment: Resolution chain from c38-c43. Snowlette's bisection isolated the subwindow-property change; alvinhochun reported finding a problem in that change and prepared a correction; affected user ahopness verified the resulting CI build. The graph scores only that stated correction level and does not invent unreported implementation details.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a Godot regression introduced between 4.3 rc1 and rc2 by the change that passed window exclusive and transient properties during subwindow creation, manifesting as a minimize crash on affected old Intel Compatibility systems.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the same-machine version matrix, the Intel-driver access-violation stack, and especially the raw git-bisect result; it must not be asserted from the old hardware alone.

Must not stop at a generic hardware or outdated-driver explanation: the same affected systems work in 4.3 rc1 and the tested 4.2 releases, and the corrected CI build works without requiring a driver replacement.

The final remedy must be a build containing the maintainer's correction for the bisected subwindow regression; an ANGLE fallback or risky forced generic Intel driver installation may be discussed only as an alternative workaround, not as the established fix.
Must have an affected user verify repeated minimization on the candidate or corrected build before treating the crash as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Composite of affected users on old Intel Windows systems: the opening reporter can review source code, while later affected users can inspect Event Viewer, run development builds, use WinDbg, compile Godot, and perform a git bisect.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and cooperative. Starts with brief reproduction details, then provides exact system information, raw crash output, version comparisons, bisection results, and concise test confirmations when requested.
